organization.name: Wortou.AI
organization.description: A cross-disciplinary AI game team spanning research, engineering, and design.
organization.thesis: Large language models can serve as native game mechanics rather than only as content generators.
working_principles: Build every demo end to end until people outside the team can play it.
Judge an AI game by whether its mechanics are interesting and its world remains coherent.
Turn reusable infrastructure and testing methods into open-source tools when possible.

projects.name: Tenure-Track Simulator
projects.summary: A career simulation in which the player tries to survive and advance as a young university faculty member. The LLM responds to player decisions instead of merely selecting from a fixed story tree.
core_mechanics: LLM-generated identity, events, student profiles, social updates, and character text
Academic career progression involving grants, papers, students, funding, and wellbeing
Player choices influence later events and possible life paths
engineering_context: The early system mixed multiple models, assigning different content-generation tasks according to quality, latency, and cost.
The project exposed practical AI-game constraints including inference latency, concurrency, token cost, analytics, and long-term state consistency.

reported_metrics.qualification: Metrics reported by the creators in a January 2026 interview.

projects.name: Fate River
projects.summary: A historical counterfactual adventure in which players inhabit historical figures and explore how different choices might alter their lives.

projects.name: Presiduck Simulator
projects.summary: A presidential simulation starring a duck, with decisions, public opinion, and unexpected events generated inside an AI-driven world.

projects.name: Just Pamper Him
projects.category: Multiplayer voice game with an AI NPC
projects.summary: Players take turns speaking with the same AI NPC and try to induce it to say their assigned keywords while contaminating the shared conversational context for opponents.

projects.name: Cyber Cricket - Poker
projects.summary: Six language models play no-limit Texas Hold'em at one table while human viewers observe their decisions, competition, and bluffing behavior.

projects.name: QuQuer Platform
projects.summary: A platform for bringing external agents into fair games, using a commit-reveal mechanism to reduce cheating and make competition auditable.

projects.name: Neuralchemy
projects.summary: A card-table experiment in which cards represent neural-network components and the browser trains a real visual model assembled from the player's hand.
core_mechanics: Buy model-component cards and upgrade compute
Assemble a network architecture from the player's hand
Train a real model in the browser and submit the result for server-side checking
Earn research points and generate lab notes from unusual runs

infrastructure_and_tools.name: FeedScription
infrastructure_and_tools.summary: The team's shared platform for AI capabilities, accounts, registration flows, and analytics across playable demos.

infrastructure_and_tools.name: KAL AI Layer
infrastructure_and_tools.summary: Reusable game components intended to help coding agents assemble complete text games quickly.

infrastructure_and_tools.name: Openovel
infrastructure_and_tools.summary: A local-first dual-loop narrative system: a foreground loop advances the story while a background agent maintains state, memory, and files.

infrastructure_and_tools.name: Fate-River Autotest
infrastructure_and_tools.summary: An automated test system in which an LLM plays a complete narrative run while the team tracks memory and strategy behavior.
